name: Klassen's Spectral Atmospheric Method
definition: A method focusing on atmospheric problems introducing spectral treatment. Each pixel color is sampled at 33 wavelengths, taking samples each 10nm, to care for the selective scattering that would be wrong using a three-coordinate color space.
summary: Klassen's Spectral Atmospheric Method simulates realistic sky color by explicitly treating spectral scattering across 33 wavelengths, distinguishing it from standard RGB approximations that fail to capture wavelength-dependent effects.
